data: Skeleton entry for /fleet (PRD-012 v0.2 / Phase A scaffold). Builder + agency + first-flight per public sources. Specs and gallery TBD in later phases.

Japan's H-IIA launched 50 successful missions between 2001 and June 2025 for JAXA's flagship missions including Hayabusa, Hayabusa2, Himawari, and SLIM. Dependable liquid-propellant workhorse that became one of the most reliable launchers ever built.
Recovered from a 5-year solar-orbit hold to achieve Venus orbit on a backup attempt; the only Venus orbiter active in its final years of operation
Second asteroid sample return (Ryugu, 2020); first artificial impact crater on an asteroid; first subsurface asteroid material returned to Earth
First precision landing within 100 m of target on another world
Japan's first Venus orbiter; recovered from a 2010 orbit-insertion failure to study cloud-top dynamics
Pinpoint lunar landing; toppled but operational
Replaces H-IIA / H-IIB at lower cost
Successor to Proton-K; modernised heavy lift
Modern Soyuz workhorse — carries Soyuz MS crew + Progress MS cargo to the ISS
Japan's staged-combustion hydrogen core, two decades of H-II service
Japan's restartable upper stage, flying from H-IIA through H3
